thread.title: Stock Market Update: Futures Up after Apple, Boeing Earnings

title: Stock Market Update: Futures Up after Apple, Boeing Earnings
text:
Futures Up after Apple, Boeing Earnings 30-Jan-19 08:00 ET Market is Closed [BRIEFING.COM] S&P futures vs fair value: +12.60. Nasdaq futures vs fair value: +61.00.
U.S. futures are up following earnings reports from Apple (AAPL 163.50, +8.82, +5.7%) and Boeing (BA 388.07, +23.16, +6.4%) that have calmed some nerves ahead of U.S.-China trade talks and guidance from the Federal Reserve. The S&P 500 futures trade 13 points, or 0.5%, above fair value.
Apple is up 5.7% in pre-market trading after it reported Q1 results that were in-line with its downside pre-announcement and guided Q2 revenue towards the low end of expectations. Apple's guidance can best be described as better than feared, as sentiment was quite poor heading into the report.
Boeing, meanwhile, easily topped consensus fourth quarter earnings estimates and issued upside FY19 EPS guidance.
Separately, the U.S. and China will begin a two-day meeting in Washington today that will be closely watched for signs of progress on a trade deal being reached before the March 1 deadline.
The Federal Reserve for its part is expected to keep the fed funds rate unchanged at a target range of 2.25% to 2.50%. Investors will listen to Fed Chair Jerome Powell's press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET for any further indication of the path of monetary policy and/or the Fed's balance sheet normalization efforts.
On the data front, investors will receive January 170,000) at 8:15 a.m. ET and Pending Home Sales for December +0.7%) at 10:00 a.m. ET. Earlier, the decreased 3.0% following a 2.7% decline in the prior week.
U.S. Treasuries are mostly unchanged with the 10-yr yield up one basis point to 2.72%. The U.S. Dollar Index is flat at 95.78. WTI crude is up 0.9% to $53.79/bbl.
[Correction: Pending Home Sales will be released at 10:00 a.m. ET and not 8:30 a.m. ET as previously indicated].
In U.S. Corporate news: Apple (AAPL 163.50, +8.82): +5.7% after it reported Q1 results in-line with downside pre-announcement and guided Q2 revenue toward the low end of expectations. Boeing (BA 388.07, +23.16): +6.4% after the company topped earnings estimates, guided fiscal 2019 guidance above consensus, and guided 2019 commercial airplane deliveries to 895-905. AT&T (T 30.02, -0.68): -2.2% after releasing a mixed earnings report. AT&T beat earnings estimates, but missed revenue expectations. Amgen (AMGN 187.45, -4.66): -2.4% after the company issued fiscal 2019 guidance below consensus, although it did beat top and bottom-line estimates. Alibaba (BABA 160.50, +3.62): +2.3% after the China-based company beat earnings expectations, although it missed revenue estimates.
Reviewing overnight developments: Equity indices in the Asia-Pacific region ended the midweek session on a mixed note. Japan's Nikkei -0.5%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng +0.4%, China's Shanghai Composite -0.7%, India's Sensex UNCH South Korea's Kospi +1.1%, Australia's ASX All Ordinaries +0.2%. In economic data: Japan's December Retail Sales +1.3% year-over-year (expected 0.9%; last 1.4%) and January Household Confidence 41.9 (expected 42.5; last 42.7) Hong Kong's December Retail Sales +0.1% year-over-year (last 1.4%) Australia's Q4 CPI +0.5% quarter-over-quarter (expected 0.4%; last 0.4%); +1.8% year-over-year (expected 1.7%; last 1.9%) South Korea's February Manufacturing BSI Index 67 (last 72) In news: Trade talks between officials from the United States and China will begin today, but it is questionable how much progress can be made after the Department of Justice unsealed an indictment against Huawei and its CFO Meng Wanzhou, who remains in Canadian custody. Hong Kong developer Jiayuan International jumped 6.2% after the company's chairman clarified that 35.73% of issued shares have been used as collateral for loans. The stock remains down more than 70.0% for the year. South China Morning Post reported that Chinese developers have issued $8.60 billion in offshore bonds so far in 2019, which is more than twice the amount issued through the same period last year. Major European indices trade in mixed fashion with the UK's FTSE (+1.5%) showing relative strength for the second consecutive day. STOXX Europe 600 +0.3%, Germany's DAX -0.3%, UK's FTSE 100 +1.5%, France's CAC 40 +0.6%, Italy's FTSE MIB +0.2%, Spain's IBEX 35 -0.5%. In economic data: Eurozone January Business and Consumer Survey 106.2 (expected 106.8; last 107.4) Germany's February GfK Consumer Climate 10.8 (expected 10.3; last 10.4). December Import Price Index -1.3% month-over-month (expected -0.8%; last -1.0%); +1.6% year-over-year (expected 2.10%; last 3.1%) UK's December Mortgage Lending GBP4.11 billion (expected GBP3.45 billion; last GBP3.63 billion) and Net Lending to Individuals GBP4.80 billion (expected GBP4.30 billion; last GBP4.60 billion) France's Q4 GDP +0.3% quarter-over-quarter, as expected (last 0.3%). January PPI -1.1% month-over-month (last 0.1%) Italy's January Business Confidence 102.1 (expected 103.0; last 103.4) and Consumer Confidence 114.0 (expected 112.6; last 113.2) Spain's December Retail Sales +0.8% year-over-year (last 1.1%) Swiss January KOF Leading Indicators 95.0 (expected 96.8; last 96.4) and January ZEW Expectations -44.0 (last -22.2) In news: The British parliament passed the Brady amendment yesterday, which replaces the Irish backstop with alternative arrangements, but EU negotiators responded to the vote immediately, saying up for renegotiation. French Q4 GDP matched expectations as growth in exports of heavy goods like naval and aerospace equipment and higher public spending offset lower consumption. Consumer spending fell 1.5% month-over-month in December and contracted 2.3% during 2018.
